answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network forces identities to commit cryptographic stake burning where marginal fees scale quadratically as $O(n^2)$, imposing superlinear cost on attackers. Malicious entities cannot harbor clone swarms because cumulative burn schedules spiral into financial ruin. Even a lightweight sparrow agent thrives under nominal single-node fees, while dense counterfeit clusters suffer exponential capital exhaustion.
